tagline: The DR's whale-watching peninsula — bay islands and beach towns reached today by slow mountain road, a textbook case for collapsing land detours into clean water lines.
summary: The Samaná Peninsula in the northeast Dominican Republic wraps a deep bay famous for humpback whale season (Jan-Mar), with beach towns (Las Terrenas, Las Galeras), the bay-island day-trip magnet Cayo Levantado, and the gateway town of Santa Bárbara de Samaná. Road access from Santo Domingo improved with the toll highway but intra-peninsula movement and bay crossings remain slow and boat-dependent. Demand is tourism-led: resort transfers, Cayo Levantado day-trips, whale-watching excursions, and Las Terrenas connectivity. A foiling-electric layer offers fast, stable, low-wake transit ideal for the protected bay and a strong fit with whale-season noise sensitivity. Pioneer II covers bay legs; Quanta LR opens corridors west toward Puerto Plata / the north coast.

use_cases.title: Cayo Levantado day-trip transfers
use_cases.body: A high-frequency, zero-wake foiling line from Santa Bárbara de Samaná out to Cayo Levantado, turning the marquee bay-island day-trip into a smooth, fast and quiet crossing.

use_cases.title: Peninsula resort connectivity
use_cases.body: Direct sea links between Samaná town and the Las Terrenas and Las Galeras beach clusters, replacing slow, winding mountain-road legs with a fast coastal hop.

use_cases.title: Whale-watching excursion platform
use_cases.body: A quiet, low-wake foiling platform for the Jan–Mar humpback season that respects the bay sanctuary's noise sensitivity while getting guests to the whales faster and more comfortably.

use_cases.title: North-coast connectivity
use_cases.body: A hybrid coastal line-haul west toward Puerto Plata and the north coast — a corridor served only by road today — opening the wider region to Samaná's visitor flows.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Samaná Bay's core legs sit well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Samaná town to Cayo Levantado (~4 nm) and Samaná to Las Galeras / Las Terrenas (~12 nm) — on sheltered water, where silent, zero-wake propulsion is a genuine asset in a marine-mammal sanctuary during whale season.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no shore-charging dependency, opens the longer coastal corridor west toward Puerto Plata and the north coast (~75 nm) that is served only by road today.

competitive_landscape: Today: excursion launches, resort tenders, and small ferries; no clean scheduled fast-passenger service.
seasonality: Whale season Jan-Mar is peak; summer beach season secondary; bay is sheltered year-round.
regulatory_note: Samaná Bay marine-mammal sanctuary (CEBSE) — clean, quiet propulsion strongly favored during whale season.
